**Write and revise your manuscript in Quarto while collaborators review Word drafts with native comments and tracked changes.**
Quarto review brings supported Word feedback into editable QMD, keeps the discussion attached to the text, and produces a Word draft with review information intact.
You can work in your preferred editor or with a coding assistant, inspect changes in HTML, and render Word when you are ready to share.

The manuscript, suggestions, comment threads and decisions live together in one working file.
A frozen reference supplies the comparison for ordinary prose edits.
Use explicit suggestions when you want to control exactly how a change is presented to collaborators.

[Get the editable example](downloads/walkthrough.zip) · [See its Word output](index.docx) · [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review)

This guide is itself a review document.
Each example pairs the source you edit with a result rendered by the extension.
All study details and reviewer names are fictional.

## The files you work with

A review project keeps the usual Quarto manuscript structure:

~~~text
manuscript/
  index.qmd        # Working text, suggestions and discussions
  reference.qmd    # Frozen comparison for this review round
  _quarto.yml     # Layout and output formats
  references.bib  # Bibliography, if your manuscript uses one
  figures/        # Ordinary manuscript assets, if needed
~~~

| File | What you do with it |
| --- | --- |
| index.qmd | Edit prose, propose wording, add or reply to comments, and record decisions. This is the authoritative working document. |
| reference.qmd | Leave it unchanged during the review round. Rendering compares the working prose against this snapshot. |
| _quarto.yml | Choose the manuscript layout, output formats and other normal Quarto settings. |
| Bibliography and figures | Maintain them as you would in any Quarto project. |

There is no separate editable review.yml in the current single-source format.
HTML and Word files are generated outputs; edits belong in index.qmd.
The extension creates local rendering support and caches, which you do not maintain as manuscript content.

Imported projects can also contain an archived original Word file under assets/review/.
Keep that archive and any adjacent review-data records in the QMD: some native formatting, objects and comment identities depend on them.
They are preserved source information rather than another draft to edit.

## Get a local preview {#work-locally}

Install Quarto and Python 3.12 or later.
Download and unzip the [editable example](downloads/walkthrough.zip), then run these commands in its folder:

~~~sh
python -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install git+https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review.git@v0.2.1
quarto-review enable
quarto preview index.qmd --to html
~~~

On Windows, activate the environment with `.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` in PowerShell.
The enable command installs rendering support into this example project.
It keeps the existing manuscript and frozen reference.
Edit index.qmd in your editor and save; the HTML preview refreshes to show the result.

To start with your own existing index.qmd instead, run this after installing the extension:

~~~sh
quarto-review init --author "Your Name"
quarto preview index.qmd --to html
~~~

Initialization adds review settings, enables rendering and freezes the initial reference.
The review author identifies your new suggestions and replies; it does not replace the manuscript's title-page author information.

## Edit prose and control the diff

### Ordinary editing

You can edit prose normally without marking every change by hand.
For example, the frozen reference contains:

~~~markdown
Participants completed a short practice session.
~~~

The working index.qmd contains:

~~~markdown
Participants completed a five-minute practice session before the task.
~~~

**Rendered result:**

Participants completed a short practice session.

The extension compares the two files and displays the difference as a suggestion.
The HTML **Original** and **Proposed** views show the alternatives; Word output represents the pending difference as native tracked changes.
Replies, authorship and comment-status edits are excluded from this prose comparison.

Keep one sentence per source line if that helps review your Markdown changes.
A normal newline remains part of the same rendered paragraph; avoid trailing spaces that request a hard line break.

### Explicit suggestions

When the grouping or attribution of a change matters, write the suggestion explicitly using CriticMarkup.
The old and proposed wording stay together, with a stable ID and author alias:

~~~markdown
The study found [a {~~large~>modest~~}{#s1 by=R} difference in recall]{#c1}.
Participants remembered more words after spaced practice{++ than after massed practice++}{#s2 by=M}.
The result was {--very --}{#s3 by=R}consistent across the two lists.
~~~

**Rendered result:**

The study found [a {~~large~>modest~~}{#s1 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:00:00Z} difference in recall]{#c1}.
Participants remembered more words after spaced practice{++ than after massed practice++}{#s2 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:05:00Z}.
The result was {--very --}{#s3 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:10:00Z}consistent across the two lists.

The three forms represent a replacement, insertion and deletion.
Pending is the default.
The surrounding span with ID c1 anchors a comment, explained in the next section.
Use a unique ID for each suggestion or message; reuse a comment ID only to connect its passage with its discussion.

Define aliases once in the QMD front matter:

~~~yaml
review:
  schema: 2
  author: A
  authors:
    A: Alex Author
    R: Robin Reviewer
    M: Morgan Reviewer
~~~

The current author is A; by=R attributes that particular suggestion to Robin.
An optional at attribute retains its date.
Commands supply dates for new review actions, and imported attribution remains attached to the original reviewer.

You can create a suggestion through a command too:

~~~sh
quarto-review suggest --text "an exact phrase" --replacement "its proposed wording"
~~~

The selected phrase must occur unambiguously in the source.
If you have already edited the wording, the group command lets you record the intended before/after replacement explicitly.
See the [source-format guide](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/single-source.md) for the full syntax.

## Add comments and replies

### A passage and its discussion

A comment has two parts in the same QMD file: a marked passage and a discussion block with the matching ID.
This is the discussion attached to the first suggested sentence above:

~~~markdown
:::: {.review-thread #c1 by=R}
Could we say **modest** here?
The estimate does not support “large”.

- Keep the direction of the result.
- Qualify its magnitude.

::: {.reply #r1 by=A}
Agreed.
I have left the replacement pending so we can compare both versions.
:::
::::
~~~

Put discussion blocks near their passages or collect them at the end of index.qmd.
Their position does not determine what they comment on: the IDs do.
Moving a complete discussion block does not create a manuscript wording change.

To reply by hand, add another reply block inside the thread with a new ID and your author alias.
A reply normally addresses the initial comment; add to=r1 to reply specifically to r1.
Alternatively, let the command create the ID, attribution and date:

~~~sh
quarto-review reply c1 --body "I agree with the revised description."
~~~

This updates index.qmd only; the next render includes the reply in HTML and Word.
You can create a new anchored comment with the comment command:

~~~sh
quarto-review comment --text "an exact passage" --body "Please explain this."
~~~

### Overlapping ranges

When two comments cover overlapping text, use explicit start and end markers:

~~~markdown
Participants completed []{#c2-start}two practice sessions []{#c3-start}one week apart[]{#c2-end}, followed by a delayed recall test[]{#c3-end}.
~~~

**Rendered result:**

Participants completed []{#c2-start}two practice sessions []{#c3-start}one week apart[]{#c2-end}, followed by a delayed recall test[]{#c3-end}.

Define c2 and c3 in separate discussion blocks, just as for c1.
In this example, Robin asks about the sessions and Morgan asks about the test timing.
Robin's thread includes Alex's reply and a further reply to it; all of that is visible in the downloadable QMD.

### Formatted and literal messages

[The reporting checklist includes the estimate, its uncertainty and the sample size]{#c5}.
A colleague also asked us to [retain a literal notation example]{#c6}.

The checklist discussion uses Markdown emphasis, a numbered list, a link and inline code.
For a message whose punctuation should remain literal, put format=plain on its opening line:

~~~markdown
:::: {.review-thread #c6 by=R format=plain}
Keep *asterisks*, _underscores_ and [brackets] exactly as written.
::::
~~~

Word imports retain that literal interpretation by default.
Authored Markdown is formatted in HTML; Word discussion bodies currently keep the stored Markdown punctuation rather than translating it into native formatting.

## Record decisions in the source

Review controls change what you see; decisions change the working QMD.
You can edit the attributes directly or use commands:

| Action | Source representation | Command |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Resolve a comment | Add .resolved to the review-thread opening line | quarto-review resolve c1 |
| Reopen a comment | Remove .resolved | quarto-review reopen c1 |
| Accept a suggestion | Add .accepted to the suggestion's attributes | quarto-review accept s1 |
| Reject a suggestion | Add .rejected to the suggestion's attributes | quarto-review reject s1 |
| Return a suggestion to pending | Remove .accepted or .rejected | quarto-review pending s1 |

For example:

~~~markdown
The task was {~~hard~>demanding~~}{#s4 by=R .accepted}.
The finding {~~suggests~>proves~~}{#s5 by=M .rejected} that spacing may improve recall.
~~~

**Rendered result:**

The task was {~~hard~>demanding~~}{#s4 by=R .accepted}.
The finding {~~suggests~>proves~~}{#s5 by=M .rejected} that spacing may improve recall.

Both text views show “demanding” and “suggests” because those decisions are already made.
The alternatives remain recorded in the source.
The comment on the [recruitment target of 40 participants]{#c4} is also resolved; its thread has .resolved on its opening line.

Resolving a discussion does not accept a nearby suggestion.
Replying does not reopen a resolved thread automatically.
To rewrite wording with a recorded decision in the same round, first return that suggestion to pending.

Use the feedback command to list review IDs, wording, authors and states:

~~~sh
quarto-review feedback
quarto-review feedback --id c1
quarto-review validate
~~~

An automatically detected prose edit also appears in feedback.
Accepting or rejecting its ID first records that edit explicitly in index.qmd, so the decision has a stable source representation.

Deletion is different from resolution.
The delete-comment command removes the discussion, its replies and its range markers while preserving the manuscript wording and other annotations.
Deleting just the discussion block would leave a dangling anchor, so use the command when removing a thread:

~~~sh
quarto-review delete-comment c1
~~~

## Render, share and start the next round

While editing, keep the HTML preview running or render it on demand:

~~~sh
quarto render index.qmd --to html
~~~

In HTML, **Redline**, **Original** and **Proposed** compare pending wording.
Review starts with Comments; select Changes to inspect suggestions, then filter their status to Pending, Accepted or Rejected.
Change cards show removed and added wording alongside the author and decision.
Previous and Next move through matching records, including accepted deletions and rejected insertions that leave no text in the manuscript.
A Δ marker locates each change while changes are selected.
Author and status filters affect the review cards without fading the manuscript's redline colours.
**Reading view** hides markup, comments and controls, and **Show review** restores them.
These are display choices and do not modify the QMD or exported Word draft.

Select layout and output formats through the normal _quarto.yml settings.
For example:

~~~yaml
project:
  type: manuscript
manuscript:
  article: index.qmd
format:
  html: default
  docx: default
~~~

The enable command adds the review integration while retaining your format settings.
This page uses Quarto's standard manuscript layout; installed styles such as APAQuarto can be selected in your own project.
Keep the bibliography, figures and other presentation settings there too.

When ready to send a draft to collaborators, render Word explicitly:

~~~sh
quarto render index.qmd --to docx
~~~

The [example Word draft](index.docx) contains native comments, replies and pending tracked changes generated from the same working source as this page.
HTML views and filters do not change what is exported.
The review list can show all matching comments and changes without moving the document.
Review defaults to comments and changes, with open comments and pending changes selected; changing review type selects the corresponding available status.

Freeze a new reference only when you deliberately begin a new review round:

~~~sh
quarto-review reference --new-round
~~~

This archives the previous reference and captures the current annotated QMD as the next baseline.
Ordinary rendering never advances the baseline.
Keep the source version corresponding to any Word draft you send so you can compare returned feedback with it.

## Bring Word feedback into the project

You can begin with collaborators' feedback in a Word document:

~~~sh
quarto-review import-docx reviewed.docx --into candidate --author "Your Name"
cd candidate
quarto-review enable
quarto preview index.qmd --to html
~~~

Import creates a new directory with a working QMD, frozen reference, extracted assets and an archive of the original Word document.
Supported comments, replies, ranges, reviewer attribution and suggested changes are retained for editing and export.
Keep the original Word assets and native review-data records that the importer supplies.

**Current boundary:** this is not automatic synchronisation between a live Word document and your QMD.
A returned Word draft is imported as a separate candidate for comparison with the version sent; the current single-source workflow does not automatically merge independently edited returns.
Word-to-Quarto conversion also does not promise identical original Word page layout.
Follow the [worked review round](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/review-round.md) for the complete comparison and application procedure, including a retained local edit.
The [installation guide](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/installation.md) describes runtime files, upgrades and removal.

See [tested compatibility and limits](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/status.md) for supported constructs and verification evidence, and the [source-format reference](https://github.com/githubpsyche/quarto-review/blob/main/docs/single-source.md) for complete syntax.

<!-- Discussion positions do not determine their anchors. -->

:::: {.review-thread #c1 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:01:00Z}
Could we say **modest** here?
The estimate does not support “large”.

- Keep the direction of the result.
- Qualify its magnitude.

::: {.reply #r1 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:00:00Z}
Agreed.
I have left the replacement pending so we can compare both versions.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c2 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:15:00Z}
Were the same word lists used in both sessions?

::: {.reply #r2 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:05:00Z}
No; each session used a different list.
:::

::: {.reply #r3 by=R at=2026-09-01T10:10:00Z to=r2}
Thanks.
Please include that distinction in the methods.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c3 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:20:00Z}
How long after the second practice session was the test?
My range overlaps Robin's, but this is a separate question about timing.
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c4 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:25:00Z .resolved}
Is this the planned or final sample?

::: {.reply #r4 by=A at=2026-09-01T10:15:00Z}
The planned sample; “recruitment target” makes that explicit.
:::
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c5 by=M at=2026-09-01T09:30:00Z}
Please include **all three**:

1. The estimated difference.
2. An uncertainty interval.
3. The analysed sample size.

Use `n` consistently for the sample size.
See [working locally](#work-locally) to reply to this discussion.
::::

:::: {.review-thread #c6 by=R at=2026-09-01T09:35:00Z format=plain}
Keep *asterisks*, _underscores_ and [brackets] exactly as written.
This synthetic message demonstrates the literal format used for imported Word text.
::::
